title: Seattle Seahawks face roster changes and injuries
seoTitle: Seattle Seahawks Face Roster Changes & Injuries
subtitle: Team seeks alternatives after major defensive losses for the season
excerpt: Get the latest Seattle Seahawks moves, including new signings and injuries impacting the defense for the team's upcoming games.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Seattle Seahawks, The New York Times
contentHtml:
The Seattle Seahawks team is undergoing roster restructuring after facing major losses due to injuries and making new moves in the market. The coaching staff is seeking solutions to maintain the defensive solidity that has characterized the team in recent seasons.

Injuries disrupt defensive planning

Safety Bud Clark will be sidelined for several months after breaking his right ankle during a preseason game against the Tennessee Titans. In addition, offensive lineman Mason Richman also suffered a serious, long-term injury in the same matchup. Another recent absence was wide receiver Jake Bobo, who was placed on the injured reserve list due to a knee issue.

New signings to fill the gaps

To fill open roster spots, the front office signed tackle Derrick Graham, safety Tysheem Johnson, and running back Justin Jones. The team also added cornerback Trevon Diggs on a one-year deal and reached an agreement with cornerback Terrion Arnold, whose paperwork is still awaiting official signature.

The situation in the secondary

Head coach Mike Macdonald emphasized that depth at the safety position will be tested with the recent absences. While players like Nick Emmanwori are working toward a return following surgery, athletes like Ty Okada are standing out in practice to fill the voids and maintain the group's competitive level on the field.

Expectations for the rest of the season

With so many changes to the group and the need to reassess available options, the Seahawks are trying to adjust their defensive strategy. The coaching staff is counting on internal competitiveness and the utilization of players like AJ Finley and D'Anthony Bell to face the upcoming challenges in the championship.

With information from Seattle Seahawks, The New York Times.
